any: Sat where Mrs Macquarie used to sit and watch for ships. From her bench the sails and the bridge line up as if somebody planned it.
dusk: The sun goes down behind the bridge from here. Everyone on the point stopped talking for about a minute.
night: The sails are lit and the bridge is a string of lamps. I stayed on the point longer than I meant to.

any: Up on the Cahill Walk, over the station. The whole quay is below, ferries in and out, and the bridge is straight ahead.
The sails are bigger than the photographs say, and not quite white: close up, the tiles are cream and they shine.
dusk: Last light on the shells. The steps were still warm when I sat down on them.

any: Under the bridge at Dawes Point. You hear a train cross before you see it, and the whole deck hums.
Circular Quay from the west side. A ferry leaves every few minutes, and each one swings past the Opera House on its way out.
A table by the sea wall at the Opera Bar, the bridge across the water. The gulls here watch every chip.
night: The bridge lit from end to end, and its lights broken up on the water. Nobody at the bar was in a hurry.
